# Behavioral Specification: Power Manager Slow Sequencer

## 1. Overview

The slow sequencer is the always-on power-management control block. It is responsible for sequencing the main power domain, power isolation clamps, and high-speed clock enables during power-up, low-power entry, and low-power exit. It also reports whether the most recent low-power exit was caused by a wakeup or by a reset request.

The sequencer has two normal resting states:

- Active/idle: main power is on, high-speed clocks are running, and the system is fully powered.
- Low power: clocks and optionally main power are turned off according to the low-power configuration, and the sequencer waits for a wakeup or reset request.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

- On reset, the sequencer shall initialize all outputs to safe values:
  - The power-up cause shall be reported as a power-on reset.
  - The cause-change toggle shall be low.
  - The main power request shall be in the on state.
  - Power isolation clamps shall be deasserted.
  - High-speed clock enable requests shall be off.
  - The power-up request to the fast-domain sequencer shall be off.
  - The power-down acknowledge shall be off.
  - The invalid-state flag shall be off.
- After reset is released, the sequencer shall automatically begin the power-on sequence. It shall not wait for software configuration.
- A separate main-domain reset input affects only the main power-good observation logic and shall not reset the main sequencer state.

## 3. Power-On Sequence

The power-on sequence shall proceed as follows:

1. Keep the main power request asserted and wait until the main power-good indication is valid.
2. Once main power-good is valid, deassert the early power isolation clamp.
3. Deassert the main power isolation clamp.
4. Enable the high-speed clocks required for active operation:
   - The core clock enable shall be asserted.
   - The I/O clock enable shall be asserted.
   - The USB clock enable shall be asserted only if the active-mode USB clock configuration requests it.
5. Wait until all clocks required for active operation report valid. A USB clock valid indication is required only when the USB clock is configured to be enabled.
6. Assert the power-up request to the fast-domain sequencer.
7. Wait until the fast-domain sequencer acknowledges the power-up request and no low-power request is pending.
8. Deassert the power-up request and enter the active/idle resting state.

In the active/idle state, the main power request shall remain asserted and the high-speed clocks shall remain running.

## 4. Low-Power Entry

Low-power entry shall begin from the active/idle state when a low-power request is received.

- The low-power request shall be accepted only when the previous power-up acknowledge is no longer asserted.
- Upon acceptance, the sequencer shall assert the power-down acknowledge.
- The power-down acknowledge shall remain asserted until the low-power request is withdrawn.
- After the low-power request is withdrawn, the power-down acknowledge shall be deasserted and the shutdown sequence shall begin.

During shutdown:

- The clock enables shall be set according to the low-power configuration.
  - If the main power domain is configured to be turned off, all high-speed clock enables shall be off.
  - If the main power domain is configured to remain on, clocks that are configured to stay enabled may remain enabled.
- The sequencer shall wait until every clock that is configured to be disabled reports invalid. Clocks configured to remain enabled are not required to report invalid.
- If the main power domain is configured to remain on:
  - Power isolation clamps shall not be asserted.
  - The main power request shall remain asserted.
  - The sequencer shall enter low power directly.
- If the main power domain is configured to be turned off:
  - The early power isolation clamp shall be asserted first.
  - The main power isolation clamp shall then be asserted.
  - The main power request shall be deasserted.
  - The sequencer shall wait until the main power-good indication deasserts.
  - The sequencer shall then enter the low-power state.

## 5. Low-Power Exit and Cause Reporting

The sequencer shall evaluate wakeup and reset requests only while in the low-power state.

- A normal wakeup shall cause the power-on sequence to begin and the power-up cause shall be reported as a wakeup.
- A reset request received in low power shall also cause the power-on sequence to begin, but the power-up cause shall be reported as a reset request.
- If both a wakeup and a reset request are present at the same time, the reset request shall take precedence.
- On every low-power exit, the cause-change toggle shall change state. This provides a way for other logic to detect that the cause information has been updated.
- The power-up cause shall remain stable throughout the resulting power-on sequence and active/idle state until the next low-power exit.

## 6. Clock Enable Control

The sequencer shall drive high-speed clock enable requests according to the current phase of operation.

- In the power-on, handshake, and active/idle phases, the core and I/O clock enables shall be forced on.
- In low power, the core and I/O clock enables shall follow the low-power configuration. If main power is off, they shall be off.
- The USB clock enable shall follow the active configuration during power-on and active operation, and the low-power configuration during low power. If main power is off, the USB clock enable shall be off.
- The USB clock-source enable shall remain asserted while the USB IP reports that its clock is still active, even if the sequencer has requested the USB clock to be disabled. This prevents the clock source from being cut before the USB IP has stopped using the clock.
- The USB IP clock enable output shall reflect the requested USB clock state.
- The always-on slow clock enable shall be asserted continuously.

## 7. Main Power Monitoring and Reset Request

The sequencer shall monitor the main power-good status in the active/idle state and in the low-power state when the main power domain is configured to remain on.

The sequencer shall track whether main power-good has been validated at least once since the last main-domain reset. This validation is performed during the normal power-on sequence.

- If the sequencer is in a state where the main power domain is expected to be on and this validation has not occurred, the sequencer shall assert a reset request.
- Once asserted, the reset request shall remain asserted until a clear request is received from the fast-domain sequencer.
- A clear request shall deassert the reset request and shall also mark the main power-good validation as satisfied.

This behavior provides a reset-escalation path for cases where the main power domain has been disturbed and has not gone through the normal power-on validation.

## 8. Handshake Behavior

The sequencer shall provide deterministic handshake behavior with the fast-domain sequencer.

- The power-up request shall be asserted only after the required clocks are valid and power clamps are off.
- The power-up request shall remain asserted until the fast domain acknowledges and no low-power request is pending.
- The power-down acknowledge shall be asserted only after accepting a low-power request.
- The power-down acknowledge shall remain asserted until the low-power request is withdrawn.

These handshakes ensure that power and clock state changes happen in the correct order and that the fast-domain sequencer can track the progress of the slow sequencer.

## 9. Invalid-State Behavior

If the sequencer enters a state that is not one of the defined operating states, it shall enter a terminal invalid behavior.

In this invalid behavior:

- The invalid-state flag shall be asserted.
- The main power request shall be deasserted.
- Both power isolation clamps shall be asserted.
- The core, I/O, and USB clock enable requests shall be forced on.

The invalid flag shall remain asserted and the sequencer shall remain in this terminal state until a power-on reset. A clear request, wakeup, or reset request shall not recover the sequencer from this state.

## 10. Power Clamp Sequencing

The power isolation clamp sequencing shall satisfy the following requirements:

- During power-on:
  - Power clamps shall not be deasserted until main power-good is valid.
  - The early clamp shall be deasserted before the main clamp.
  - High-speed clock enables shall not be asserted until the clamps are deasserted.
- During power-down with main power off:
  - Clocks shall be confirmed off before power clamps are asserted.
  - The early clamp shall be asserted before the main clamp.
  - Main power shall not be deasserted until both clamps are asserted.
  - The sequencer shall not enter low power until main power-good has deasserted.
- During low-power entry with main power on:
  - Power clamps shall remain deasserted.
  - Main power shall remain asserted.

## 11. Summary of Outputs

The sequencer shall provide the following observable outputs:

- A main power request that is on during normal operation and off in deep low power.
- Power isolation clamp requests for both the early/main isolation stages.
- Clock enable requests for core, I/O, and USB clocks.
- A request/acknowledge interface for coordinating power-up with the fast-domain sequencer.
- A power-down acknowledge for low-power entry coordination.
- A power-up cause value indicating power-on reset, wakeup, or reset request.
- A cause-change toggle that changes on every low-power exit.
- A reset request for main power instability.
- An invalid-state flag indicating that the sequencer has entered its terminal invalid state.
- A continuously asserted slow clock enable.
